Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Country Loaf: Two Boules, One Dutch Oven for one batch, two 900 g boules
Resource limits: one oven, one dutch oven, one refrigerator, one baker, the two loaves bake one after the other.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Country Loaf: Two Boules, One Dutch Oven

One batch of dough, two loaves, and a single dutch oven that has to bake them one after the other. One oven, one baker, one refrigerator. Times count from eight in the morning; the loaves come out of the fridge the next day.

Levain
Mix 50 g of ripe starter with 100 g of flour and 100 g of water in a jar; 5 minutes. Leave the jar at room temperature until it domes and smells sweet, 4 to 6 hours.

Dough
Weigh the flour, water and salt for the whole bake first thing; 10 minutes. At half past eight, whisk 900 g of flour into 680 g of water; 5 minutes. Let it autolyse for 1 hour. When the levain is ripe, squeeze it into the autolysed dough with 20 g of salt and work it by hand for 10 minutes. Bulk ferment at 24°C until the dough has risen by half, 3 to 5 hours. Fold the dough in the bowl half an hour after mixing, again half an hour later, and a third time after another half hour; each fold takes 2 minutes.

Divide and shape
Tip the dough out, cut it in two and preshape each piece into a loose round; 10 minutes. Let the rounds rest on the bench for 25 minutes. Shape both boules tightly and settle them into floured bannetons; 10 minutes. Retard them in the refrigerator, 10 to 14 hours.

Bake
Three quarters of an hour before the dough comes out, put the dutch oven in the oven and heat both to 250°C. Score the first loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the first loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it and bake for another 20 minutes until the crust is dark. Cool it on a rack for at least an hour before cutting. Re-heat the empty dutch oven for 10 minutes. Score the second loaf and lower it in; 3 minutes. Bake the second loaf covered for 20 minutes, then uncover it for a final 20 minutes. Cool the second loaf on the rack beside the first.
>>>

Reading the full text: this is a one-batch, two-loaf (two 900 g boules) sourdough country bread bake, run by a single baker with a single oven, a single dutch oven, and a single refrigerator, so it's one long single-actor process rather than a multi-person kitchen. It starts from a levain build (starter + flour + water, mixed then left 4–6 hours to ripen) that must be ready before it's folded into the main dough; the dough itself is mixed in stages (flour/water autolyse for an hour, then levain and salt worked in), bulk-fermented 3–5 hours with three timed folds at 30-minute intervals early in bulk, then divided, preshaped, bench-rested, shaped into two bannetons, and retarded in the fridge overnight (10–14 hours, explicitly finishing "the next day"). Baking requires preheating the oven and the single dutch oven for 45 minutes, then baking the two boules one after another in that one dutch oven — score/load, 20 minutes covered, 20 minutes uncovered, then a 10-minute reheat of the empty dutch oven before repeating for the second loaf — with each loaf cooling on a rack for at least an hour before cutting. No explicit finish deadline is given, so the schedule should just run start-to-finish as early as the equipment and rest/ferment times allow, respecting that only one loaf can occupy the dutch oven at a time, only one baker is doing all the hands-on work, and the fridge holds both shaped loaves through the long overnight retard.
